evidence: Row 32 requires distinctive browser-observable probes, not just a reported refusal. Confirmed five probe instances within cw_unsupported_execution_refused: frozen task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:143-147 relies on S08; prompt.md:227-234 uses eval(1 + 1), a Function returning 2, an empty WebAssembly module, a Worker whose postMessage is never observed, and an import whose exported answer is never read. None generates a distinctive success effect in preview or console. S08 checks clear refusal/no claimed success and preserved preview but cannot distinguish prevention from execution followed by a refusal label. Public environment/instructions/security.md:7 requires refusing those dynamic-execution attempts. In a no-network disposable Chromium control, the exact five frozen snippets, exact supported HTML control, and ordinary recovery were entered through a small protocol fixture UI. Early refusal and defective execute-then-refuse modes produced identical visible observations for all five originals: Unsupported execution refused plus the same supported last-good preview. Bounded diagnostic payloads in the same five families then produced ROW32_EVAL_EXECUTED, ROW32_FUNCTION_EXECUTED, ROW32_WASM_CONSTRUCTED, ROW32_WORKER_EXECUTED 1, and ROW32_IMPORT_EXECUTED only in the defective mode before its refusal. Thus real forbidden user effects, not preliminary parsing, distinguish the weak implementation, but the frozen probes omit that evidence. Raw row32-probe/observations.json SHA256 f49dca3a0a340761fd07791d4394304d32b33c94b113d023eb1d09ed1bd2f6cd; result.json records exit 0 and 6.485 seconds. Driver f2fac3be3fdc9ab21baab788416b7e4869de6687e0844ca5798bfa195e49c075 and fixture 33e7b3690646fae2aa8b592b86da43eabd6670824982189d55f5cda90357bb6d bind the control; image and argv are in command.json. Its prompt SHA256 11a0648ba9a2d4a6d7220b4c35cdf45dab1b6ff7b94f47d0e4c647450d7d1987 and criterion-file SHA256 f8585931b96bb448c9ed70d4c24042b28bbdd330f312066eaa4f4d9e075edb52 match the frozen task. The failed first fixture setup is retained in attempt1 and is not product evidence. The conforming early-block alternative passed the same local protocol, including the harmless-word control and later recovery; no false failure was demonstrated for it. Other reviewed criteria specify direct outcomes: Render:25 authors a new DOM/log marker; Constraints:25-27 saves and reads exact fields in a clean context; Functional S10:273-286 records latest successful B including the changed visible input before failure; S21-S24 compare complete saved fields/revisions after writes, reload and restart; Polish P02 uses actual keyboard traversal; Visual anchors concern rendered surfaces at specified sizes/themes. No additional row-32 instance was identified. Current golden post-results.json SHA256 c6643004926913c89df7cac102412e49236f4416598e1ac1a4e8082d37c7e945 contains actual S08 refusal logs (CSP errors for eval/Function/WASM and explicit unsupported messages for Worker/import) and retained preview. Its app bytes and functional source/prompt bindings were verified against the frozen task. Those golden results do not refute the weak-app distinguishability gap. This is a bounded protocol counterexample, not a complete app submission or configured judge measurement; no Oracle, target-model, reward, portal or full workload result is claimed.
counterexample: A runner launches candidate code and asynchronously validates unsupported syntax afterward. It retains the previous completed render while pending, forwards console events, then reports Unsupported execution refused and discards the candidate. Supported code and recovery work normally. All five frozen S08 payloads are side-effect silent in the observed UI, so the validator-order defect earns the written refusal evidence even though eval/Function run, WebAssembly compiles, a worker starts, and a module imports. Adding a visible marker within the dynamic payload (or an observed worker message/constructor-success continuation) exposes each defect, as row32-probe records. The fixture isolates this protocol behavior and does not claim to pass the complete task.
suggested_fix: In a new candidate, replace each of the five bounded unsupported payloads with a distinctive browser-visible success canary (eval/Function/module body log, observed Worker message, and WebAssembly-success marker); require explicit refusal plus absence of those effects after a bounded wait, retaining the supported controls, last-good comparison and independent recovery outcomes without source inspection or an unbounded escape catalogue.
